summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease, prior CABG, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and a previous stroke was admitted after a mechanical fall at home two days prior. She reported no loss of consciousness or pre-syncopal symptoms but described chronic dizziness and gait instability. Evaluation included a normal head CT and EKG, negative cardiac enzymes, and no orthostatic hypotension, ruling out acute neurological or cardiac causes. She was found to have contusions to the head, shoulder, and leg but no fractures. Physical therapy recommended a cane and outpatient rehabilitation for balance and strength. Her diabetes was poorly controlled with admission glucose in the 200s and a recent A1c of 8.5%; her insulin regimen was simplified to 70/30 insulin twice daily with sliding scale coverage. She was discharged home with instructions to use a cane, attend physical therapy, adhere to her new insulin regimen, and follow up with her primary care provider.
